$comment: The detail framing of the Sarajevo motorcade photograph of 28 June 1914; the sibling directory carries the other framing of the same exposure.

original.description: A close view of the car's occupants: at the left the driver and an officer in a black peaked cap, then a general officer in a white-plumed cocked hat, an officer in a peaked cap, a man in grey seen from behind holding a parasol, and at the right Sophie in a white hat with a corsage beside Franz Ferdinand in the light blue tunic and green-plumed helmet of an Austro-Hungarian general.
original.photographer: not identified in the catalogue record
original.archive: Imperial War Museums, catalogue number Q 91848 — 'Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo, June 1914', the couple leaving the City Hall by motor car; also held, in other copies, by the Historical Archives of Sarajevo
original.licence: public domain — PD-UKGov for the IWM copy (UK Government work created before 1 June 1957); the photograph itself dates from 1914 and is out of copyright in its country of origin

colorization.author: Dave Tashner / Sandtable
colorization.method: AI-assisted colorization from the public-domain original, 2026
colorization.licence: Sandtable project licence; underlying photograph public domain
colorization.status: ok — label 'colorized (AI-assisted)'. Documented colours: the pike-grey Austro-Hungarian general officers' tunic, the green plume of a general's helmet, Sophie's white summer dress and hat, the dark lacquer of the car. The plume and facing colours are the colorizer's reading rather than matched to a reference — flag for the image review (sand-y0u.7).

content_policy: ok — the couple alive and in the car; the assassination itself is not shown and no such image belongs in the pack
caption: Sophie and Franz Ferdinand in the back of the car at Sarajevo, 28 June 1914 — the last hour of both their lives, and the first link in the chain that followed. Colorized (AI-assisted) from a public-domain photograph.
credit: Original photograph: photographer not identified, Sarajevo, 28 June 1914; Imperial War Museums Q 91848, via Wikimedia Commons; public domain. Colorization: Sandtable, AI-assisted, 2026.
notes: Supplied by Dave 2026-08-23. IDENTIFICATION: matched to the IWM record by content — the car, the occupants and the building all correspond to Q 91848, the departure from Sarajevo City Hall. The framing here is detail and its aspect ratio differs from the IWM copy (this file 1.459 against the IWM copy's 1.233), so it derives from a different and less tightly cropped reproduction of the same exposure, whose particular scan is not identified. The sibling manifest holds the other framing. For the image review (sand-y0u.7): confirm the moment — several similar photographs were taken that morning, on the arrival at the City Hall as well as the departure. Intended placement: the July Crisis chain (sand-1l0.23, shipped in PR #60) and the Sarajevo backstory (sand-1l0.32, in flight).
